In a school, there is N total number of students in classes 10th, 11th, and 12th. 45% of the total students are in class 10th and the ratio of the number of students in class 10th to class 12th is 5:3. The ratio of boys to girls in class 11th is 9:5 and 40% of the total students in class 10th are girls. There is a total of 246 girls in three classes and 50 girls in class 12th.

Question: The number of boys in class 12th is how much more than the number of girls in class 11th?
questions.explanation:
Given total number of students \(= N\)

Total number of students in class 10th \(= 0.45N\)

Then number of students in class 12th \(= \frac{0.45 \times 3}{5}N = 0.27N\)

\(\Rightarrow N = \frac{196}{0.28} = 700\ \)

Number of boys in class 12th \(= 0.27 \times 700 - 50 = 139\)

Number of girls in class 11th \(= 0.1 \times 700 = 70\)

Difference \(= 139 - 70 = 69\)

questions.question: Thief and the police were at same place and the thief started running after seeing the police and he went 200 m ahead when police got notice. Police also started running to chase the thief and the speed of police and thief are 54 kmph and 36 kmph respectively, then find the time taken by the police to chase the thief in seconds.
questions.explanation:
Speed of police \(= 54 \times \frac{5}{18}\  = 15\ m\ /s\)

Speed of thief \(= \ 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\ km/hr\)

Relative speed of police and thief \(= 15 - 10 = \ 5\ m/s\)

Total Time taken by police to catch thief\(= \frac{200\ m}{5} = 40\ sec\)
